title: Moussaka
subtitle: Layered lamb and aubergine bake with bechamel
excerpt: Layers of roasted aubergine and spiced lamb mince topped with a thick, egg-enriched bechamel and baked until deeply golden. The aubergine must be roasted separately first so it gives up its moisture and develops flavour before layering. This takes time but most of it is hands-off oven work.
sourceNotes: Moussaka is found across the Eastern Mediterranean and Balkans, but the layered Greek version with bechamel topping was formalised by French-trained Greek chef Nikolaos Tselementes in the early 20th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The lamb layer and roasted aubergine can be prepared a day ahead. Assemble and bake on the day. The assembled unbaked dish can be refrigerated for up to 8 hours; add 10 minutes to the bake time.

content.text: Salt the aubergine slices and leave them for 20 minutes before roasting. This draws out excess moisture and prevents a watery bake. Pat them dry before they go in the oven. The bechamel is enriched with egg yolks, which give the top layer a richer, more custardy set than a standard white sauce. Let the finished moussaka rest for at least 15 minutes before cutting; it holds together far better once it has settled.

items.prepNote: sliced 1cm thick, salted and patted dry

content.text: Heat the oven to 200C (fan 180C). Lay the salted and dried aubergine slices on one or two oiled baking trays. Brush with 3 tbsp olive oil. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and completely soft, flipping once. Set aside. Reduce oven to 180C (fan 160C / Gas 4).

Make the lamb layer: heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pan. Brown the lamb mince in batches over a high heat, breaking it up. Remove and set aside. In the same pan, soften the onion for 6 minutes, then add garlic, tomato puree, cinnamon, allspice and oregano. Cook 1 minute. Add tinned tomatoes and the browned mince. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Season.

Make the bechamel: melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the warm milk, a little at a time, until smooth. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick. Remove from heat. Whisk in the egg yolks and parmesan. Season.

Assemble: spread half the lamb mixture in the base of a large baking dish (roughly 30 x 22cm). Layer half the aubergine slices over the top. Repeat with the remaining lamb and aubergine. Pour the bechamel evenly over the surface.
Bake at 180C for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden and set. Rest for at least 15 minutes before slicing. It holds together much better when given time to settle.

items.symptom: Bechamel top is browning too fast before the inside is set
items.cause: Oven temperature too high or the bechamel layer was too thin
items.fix: Loosely cover with foil for the last 10 minutes and remove to allow browning. Next time ensure the bechamel is at least 2cm thick.

items.cause: Not rested long enough after baking
items.fix: Rest for at least 15 minutes, or up to 30, before cutting. The bechamel needs time to firm up once out of the oven.
